title: Longest Common Subsequence
hints: 2-D dynamic programming over positions in both strings.
`dp[i][j]` = LCS of the suffixes starting at `i` and `j`; fill from the end backwards.
jsBridge: Classic 2-D DP, converting both strings to `[Character]` first so you can index by `Int`, which Swift strings don't allow. The DP table is `[[Int]]`, the same as in JS.

compass.q: In JS you'd index `a[i-1]` directly. Why must Swift convert to `[Character]`, and what does it cost?
Full 2-D table vs two rolling rows: memory O(nm) vs O(min(n,m)). When does it matter?
Should emoji and accented characters compare as graphemes or as scalars in a diff?
LCS powers text diffing. Swift has `CollectionDifference` (`a.difference(from: b)`). Try it on two arrays.
